person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: TWO DIAGNOSTIC DEFINITIONS RUN OVER THE SAME 75,880 PEOPLE - the 2018 American Diabetes Association criteria and the World Health Organization criteria, differing by the inclusion of HbA1c, producing 12.8% and 11.2% prevalence from one national survey
span.quote: This large national survey indicated that 11.2% of adults (according to WHO criteria) or 12.8% of adults (ADA criteria including the addition of HbA 1c ) aged 18 and older living in China had diabetes in 2017. Thus the total number of patients with diabetes in mainland China is estimated to be 129.8 million (70.4 million men and 59.4 million women).

span.label: what the prevalence of diabetes and prediabetes is in mainland China, and how much of the measured rise since 2007 is the disease and how much is the criteria
span.quote: The increase in prevalence could also be partially attributable to the new diagnostic criteria, with reduced cut-off points for blood glucose and the addition of glycated haemoglobin (HbA 1c ). The American Diabetes Association (ADA) criteria and World Health Organization (WHO) criteria are shown in table 1 . The main difference between them is the inclusion of HbA 1c in the ADA criteria.

span.label: a nationally representative prevalence estimate reported under BOTH criteria from the same participants, with a like-for-like WHO-criteria series back to 2007 and provincial, ethnic and urban-rural breakdowns
span.quote: The weighted prevalence of total diabetes (n=9772), self-reported diabetes (n=4464), newly diagnosed diabetes (n=5308), and prediabetes (n=27 230) diagnosed by the ADA criteria were 12.8% (95% confidence interval 12.0% to 13.6%), 6.0% (5.4% to 6.7%), 6.8% (6.1% to 7.4%), and 35.2% (33.5% to 37.0%), respectively, among adults living in China. The weighted prevalence of total diabetes was higher among adults aged 50 and older and among men. The prevalence of total diabetes in 31 provinces ranged from 6.2% in Guizhou to 19.9% in Inner Mongolia. Han ethnicity had the highest prevalence of diabetes (12.8%) and Hui ethnicity had the lowest (6.3%) among five investigated ethnicities. The weighted prevalence of total diabetes (n=8385) using the WHO criteria was 11.2% (95% confidence interval 10.5% to 11.9%).

span.label: a disease whose presence is decided by cut-offs on continuous blood measurements, so that the count of people who have it moves when the cut-offs or the assays change
span.quote: The increase in prevalence could also be partially attributable to the new diagnostic criteria, with reduced cut-off points for blood glucose and the addition of glycated haemoglobin (HbA 1c ). The American Diabetes Association (ADA) criteria and World Health Organization (WHO) criteria are shown in table 1 . The main difference between them is the inclusion of HbA 1c in the ADA criteria.

span.label: a multistage stratified national survey (TIDE) across all 31 provinces, 2015-2017, with fasting glucose, a two-hour oral glucose tolerance test and HbA1c measured once in each participant
span.term: a multistage stratified national survey (TIDE) across all 31 provinces, 2015-2017, with fasting glucose, a two-hour oral glucose tolerance test and HbA1c measured once in each participant
span.quote: This epidemiological study, the Thyroid disorders, Iodine status and Diabetes Epidemiological survey (TIDE study), included all 31 provinces of mainland China with a sample of 75 880 people according to the age and sex composition of each community and the urban-rural ratio using the latest national census data. The study was conducted between 2015 and 2017.

span.label: **THE SAME PEOPLE, TWO DEFINITIONS, 1.6 PERCENTAGE POINTS APART**: `This large national survey indicated that 11.2% OF ADULTS (ACCORDING TO WHO CRITERIA) OR 12.8% OF ADULTS (ADA CRITERIA INCLUDING THE ADDITION OF HbA1c) aged 18 and older living in China had diabetes in 2017. Thus the total number of patients with diabetes in mainland China is estimated to be 129.8 MILLION.` **One survey, one blood draw, two answers** - and on a population this size the gap between them is on the order of eighteen million adults. simonneau2018 moved a threshold and did not estimate who it admitted; this paper simply reports both
span.quote: This large national survey indicated that 11.2% of adults (according to WHO criteria) or 12.8% of adults (ADA criteria including the addition of HbA 1c ) aged 18 and older living in China had diabetes in 2017. Thus the total number of patients with diabetes in mainland China is estimated to be 129.8 million (70.4 million men and 59.4 million women).

span.label: **AND THE PAPER SAYS THE TREND IS PARTLY THE DEFINITION, IN ITS INTRODUCTION**: `THE INCREASE IN PREVALENCE COULD ALSO BE PARTIALLY ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE NEW DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA, WITH REDUCED CUT-OFF POINTS FOR BLOOD GLUCOSE AND THE ADDITION OF GLYCATED HAEMOGLOBIN (HbA1c) ... THE MAIN DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THEM IS THE INCLUSION OF HbA1c IN THE ADA CRITERIA.` **The rise in a disease is stated as partly an artefact of how the disease is defined**, by the people measuring the rise
span.quote: The increase in prevalence could also be partially attributable to the new diagnostic criteria, with reduced cut-off points for blood glucose and the addition of glycated haemoglobin (HbA 1c ). The American Diabetes Association (ADA) criteria and World Health Organization (WHO) criteria are shown in table 1 . The main difference between them is the inclusion of HbA 1c in the ADA criteria.

span.label: **THE HEADLINE HISTORICAL SERIES CROSSES TWO RULERS MID-WAY**: `The prevalence of diabetes in adults living in China INCREASED FROM 0.67% USING THE WHO CRITERIA IN 1980 TO 10.9% USING THE ADA CRITERIA IN 2013.` A sixteenfold rise reported across a change of diagnostic criteria, with both criteria named in the same sentence. The paper's own caveat about differing sampling and screening methods follows immediately and is OUTSIDE THIS SPAN - it is separated from this clause by a run of seven citation numbers in the staged text.
span.quote: The prevalence of diabetes in adults living in China increased from 0.67% using the WHO criteria in 1980 to 10.9% using the ADA criteria in 2013.

span.label: AND THE LIKE-FOR-LIKE SERIES IS PRINTED SEPARATELY, WHICH IS THE REPAIR: `The weighted prevalence of total diabetes DIAGNOSED BY THE WHO CRITERIA has been INCREASING FROM 9.7% IN 2007 AND 2010, TO 10.4% IN 2013, AND TO 11.2% IN THIS STUDY IN 2017 ... The prevalence of prediabetes was 35.2%, which was SIMILAR TO THE 35.7% REPORTED IN 2013 WITH THE SAME ADA DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA.` **Every comparison in the discussion names which criteria it holds fixed** - `under the same WHO diagnostic criteria`, `with the same ADA diagnostic criteria`. That phrase is the whole methodological contribution
span.quote: The weighted prevalence of total diabetes diagnosed by the WHO criteria has been increasing from 9.7% in 2007 and 2010, to 10.4% in 2013, and to 11.2% in this study in 2017 (supplementary table 4). 11 12 13 The prevalence of prediabetes was 35.2%, which was similar to the 35.7% reported in 2013 with the same ADA diagnostic criteria.

span.label: **AND THE SURVEY DEFINITION IS NOT THE CLINICAL ONE, WITH THE DIRECTION OF THE ERROR NAMED**: `we did not carry out repeat testing in people with abnormal glucose values over time. WE CATEGORISED ONE READING AS BEING SYNONYMOUS WITH DIABETES, WHICH MAY OVERESTIMATE THE PREVALENCE, COMPARED WITH CLINICAL PRACTICE.` donnelly2019 says a research definition must not guide care; **this says the research definition and the clinical one give different answers, and which way**
span.quote: Fourthly, we did not carry out repeat testing in people with abnormal glucose values over time. We categorised one reading as being synonymous with diabetes, which may overestimate the prevalence, compared with clinical practice.

span.label: AND A THRESHOLD IS FLAGGED AS IMPORTED FROM ANOTHER POPULATION: `using levels of 6.5% for HbA1c to diagnose diabetes COULD BE CONTROVERSIAL SINCE THAT LEVEL WAS SET FOR THE US POPULATION. Although GEOGRAPHIC DISPARITIES MIGHT EXIST IN HbA1c LEVELS, A CONSISTENT THRESHOLD WAS PREFERRED ACROSS THE STUDY TO ENABLE COMPARISON.` **The choice is comparability over local validity, and it is stated as a choice** - which is the same trade parks2021 makes for species and polman2011 refuses for CSF status
span.quote: Secondly, using levels of 6.5% for HbA 1c to diagnose diabetes could be controversial since that level was set for the US population. Although geographic disparities might exist in HbA 1c levels, a consistent threshold was preferred across the study to enable comparison.

span.label: AND THE GEOGRAPHIC SPREAD DWARFS THE DEFINITIONAL GAP: `In Inner Mongolia, the prevalence of total diabetes was THREE TIMES HIGHER THAN THAT IN GUIZHOU PROVINCE. For prediabetes, Yunnan province had the highest prevalence, being THREE TIMES HIGHER than the lowest prevalence in Anhui province.` 6.2% to 19.9% across provinces against 11.2% versus 12.8% across definitions. **Both are real, and only one of them is usually reported as uncertainty**
span.quote: Among the 31 provinces of mainland China, a large variation in the prevalence of diabetes and prediabetes was found. In Inner Mongolia, the prevalence of total diabetes was three times higher than that in Guizhou province. For prediabetes, Yunnan province had the highest prevalence, being three times higher than the lowest prevalence in Anhui province.

span.label: AND THE ETHNIC DIFFERENCES ARE MEASURED AGAINST ONE REFERENCE GROUP: `the prevalence of total diabetes and prediabetes in FOUR ETHNIC GROUPS WAS SIGNIFICANTLY DIFFERENT FROM THAT IN THE HAN ETHNIC GROUP. Compared with the Han ethnic group, THE TIBETAN ETHNIC GROUP HAD A SIGNIFICANTLY LOWER PREVALENCE OF DIABETES.` Han 12.8%, Hui 6.3% - a twofold range inside one country, under one definition, in one survey
span.quote: This study found that the prevalence of total diabetes and prediabetes in four ethnic groups was significantly different from that in the Han ethnic group. Compared with the Han ethnic group, the Tibetan ethnic group had a significantly lower prevalence of diabetes, which was consistent with the findings of a previous study.

span.label: AND A HISTORICAL EXPOSURE IS OFFERED FOR THE AGE GRADIENT: `One study showed that PRENATAL EXPOSURE TO FAMINE MARKEDLY INCREASED THE RISK OF HYPERGLYCAEMIA IN TWO CONSECUTIVE GENERATIONS of adults living in China. Given that the CHINESE FAMINE OF 1959-61 was among the most severe on record, the affected population comprises those with a CURRENT AGE OF 50 AND OLDER, who showed a higher prevalence.` The paper adds `WHETHER OR NOT PRENATAL EXPOSURE TO FAMINE AFFECTS DIABETES REMAINS CONTROVERSIAL`
span.quote: One study showed that prenatal exposure to famine markedly increased the risk of hyperglycaemia in two consecutive generations of adults living in China. Given that the Chinese famine of 1959–61 was among the most severe on record, the affected population comprises those with a current age of 50 and older, who showed a higher prevalence of diabetes and prediabetes.

span.label: AND THE RURAL RISE IS TWO AND A HALF TIMES THE URBAN ONE, UNDER ONE DEFINITION: `Compared with the national study conducted in 2013, the current prevalence of diabetes INCREASED BY 1% IN URBAN AREAS BUT BY 2.5% IN RURAL AREAS UNDER THE SAME ADA DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA.` **`Under the same criteria` is what makes the comparison mean anything**, and the paper says it every time
span.quote: Compared with the national study conducted in 2013, the current prevalence of diabetes increased by 1% in urban areas but by 2.5% in rural areas under the same ADA diagnostic criteria.

span.label: AND AWARENESS AND PREVALENCE MOVE IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS INSIDE ONE TOTAL: `Although a CONTINUING INCREASE IN SELF-REPORTED DIABETES was found, A DECREASE IN THE PREVALENCE OF NEWLY DIAGNOSED DIABETES was noted UNDER THE SAME WHO DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA ..., suggesting BETTER AWARENESS of diabetes.` **The same total can rise while its two components move apart**, and only the split shows that the health system changed rather than the disease
span.quote: Although a continuing increase in self-reported diabetes was found, a decrease in the prevalence of newly diagnosed diabetes was noted under the same WHO diagnostic criteria (supplementary table 4), suggesting better awareness of diabetes than found in previous studies.

span.label: **ONE READING IS TREATED AS THE DISEASE**: `we did not carry out repeat testing in people with abnormal glucose values over time. WE CATEGORISED ONE READING AS BEING SYNONYMOUS WITH DIABETES, WHICH MAY OVERESTIMATE THE PREVALENCE, COMPARED WITH CLINICAL PRACTICE.` The `what is already known` box says the same of the whole literature: `SUCH SURVEYS GENERALLY USE A SINGLE READING ..., RATHER THAN REPEAT READINGS WHICH ARE TYPICAL IN CLINICAL PRACTICE`. **Every national prevalence figure for this disease is computed under a definition nobody uses on a patient**
span.quote: Fourthly, we did not carry out repeat testing in people with abnormal glucose values over time. We categorised one reading as being synonymous with diabetes, which may overestimate the prevalence, compared with clinical practice.

span.label: AND THE SAME IS TRUE OF THE WHOLE SURVEY LITERATURE, IN THE PAPER'S OWN `WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN` BOX: `SUCH SURVEYS GENERALLY USE A SINGLE READING OF GLUCOSE OR HbA1c, RATHER THAN REPEAT READINGS WHICH ARE TYPICAL IN CLINICAL PRACTICE, where clinical diagnosis is based also on patient symptoms.` **Every national prevalence figure for this disease is computed under a definition nobody uses on a patient**, and the paper states it as background rather than as its own limitation
span.quote: Such surveys generally use a single reading of glucose or HbA 1c , rather than repeat readings which are typical in clinical practice, where clinical diagnosis is based also on patient symptoms

span.label: AND THE HbA1c CUT-OFF WAS SET ELSEWHERE: `using levels of 6.5% for HbA1c to diagnose diabetes COULD BE CONTROVERSIAL SINCE THAT LEVEL WAS SET FOR THE US POPULATION.` HbA1c is the ONLY difference between the two criteria, so **the entire 1.6-point gap rests on a threshold imported from another population**
span.quote: Secondly, using levels of 6.5% for HbA 1c to diagnose diabetes could be controversial since that level was set for the US population. Although geographic disparities might exist in HbA 1c levels, a consistent threshold was preferred across the study to enable comparison.

span.label: AND A SIXTH OF THE COUNTRY IS OUTSIDE THE SAMPLE, IN A DIRECTION THE PAPER NAMES: `non-residents, such as INTERNAL MIGRANT WORKERS, WHO ACCOUNT FOR MORE THAN A SIXTH OF THE NATION'S TOTAL POPULATION and who were MORE LIKELY TO HAVE A LOWER PREVALENCE of diabetes, WERE NOT INCLUDED IN THE STUDY owing to the study design. THESE LIMITATIONS COULD LEAD TO AN OVERESTIMATION OF DIABETES IN THE POPULATION.` **Both named biases push the same way**, and the paper adds them up out loud
span.quote: Lastly, non-residents, such as internal migrant workers, who account for more than a sixth of the nation’s total population in China and who were more likely to have a lower prevalence of diabetes, were not included in the study owing to the study design. 30 31 These limitations could lead to an overestimation of diabetes in the population.

span.label: AND THE COMPARABILITY THAT MAKES THE SERIES WORK IS ITSELF A DESIGN CHOICE: `a SIMILAR STUDY DESIGN AND STATISTICAL METHODS TO THOSE USED PREVIOUSLY make our findings MORE COMPARABLE WITH HISTORICAL DATA. Although LACKING A HIGH QUALITY NATIONAL COHORT TO ESTIMATE THE INCIDENCE of diabetes, our findings could add value to the assessment of diabetes epidemics.` **A series of cross-sections is not an incidence**, and the trend is a difference of prevalences rather than a measured flow
span.quote: Secondly, a similar study design and statistical methods to those used previously make our findings more comparable with historical data. Although lacking a high quality national cohort to estimate the incidence of diabetes, our findings could add value to the assessment of diabetes epidemics in mainland China.

THE MAIN DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THEM IS THE INCLUSION OF HbA1c IN THE ADA CRITERIA.` **The cleanest natural experiment on a definition in the corpus**: same people, same day, same laboratory, two answers - and the paper reports both rather than choosing
